- (2026-01-25) The court is a place of strong passions where insults can turn to rage in a moment. Protocol matters: a politely raised hand must be called on.
- (2026-01-25) Its influence extends across the Feywild and out into the multiverse.
- (2026-01-25) Titania has the power, and Oberon is king in a lowercase sense.
- (2026-01-25) Court nobles debated whether Mona's necrotic outburst came from an astral conjunction at her birth or from an Unseelie spy hiding a darker nature.

chunks.title: Whisperwood
chunks.text:
Location: Whisperwood (first seen 2026-01-25, last seen 2026-01-25)
Also known as: Westwood, Whisper Wood
Type: domain
Parent: Feywild
Description: Independent archfey domain of Aurelia: a vast tree whose branches are the ground, with tunnel halls in its bark; an information economy of tiny and small fey.
- (2026-01-25) Whisperwood is an enormous tree. Its ground is moss on huge branches, and travel runs along branches and through wormhole tunnels in a bark about a mile thick.
- (2026-01-25) The domain is mostly filled with tiny and small creatures such as pixies, sprites, birds and squirrels, who report what they see. It runs on an information economy.
- (2026-01-25) A blight is spreading in Whisperwood. Plants turn dark brown, black and purple with blood-red veins, and resemble the plant life of the Feydark. Portia's detect poison and disease found a magical contagion.
- (2026-01-25) Aurelia's court lies inside the bark, with golden winged serpents flying through dappled sunlight. The domain refuses to join either the Seelie or Unseelie court.
- (2026-01-25) Monarch is welcome in Whisperwood, which leaves the Feywild from time to time and comes to the Prime Material. The Prime Material crossing the party used came out in a grove outside Roma.

chunks.title: Aurelia's Court
chunks.text:
Location: Aurelia's Court (first seen 2026-01-25, last seen 2026-01-25)
Also known as: court of the singing serpents
Type: hall
Parent: Whisperwood
Description: Hall in the bark of Whisperwood where Aurelia, mother of mirrors, holds court among golden serpents who are all reflections of her.
- (2026-01-25) Every member of Aurelia's close court is a reflection of herself, so speaking to the queen may mean speaking to a reflection.
- (2026-01-25) In the court Aurelia took Monarch's reflection from a mirror to stay and converse. Portia proved to be a reflection of Aurelia, who absorbed her.

chunks.title: Dragon's Lair (Najik sea caves)
chunks.text:
Location: Dragon's Lair (Najik sea caves) (first seen 2026-02-08, last seen 2026-02-08)
Also known as: the dragon's lair, dragon lair
Type: lair
Parent: Najik
Description: Skalanthas's private space in the flooded sea caves south of the monastery; nobody goes there but family
- (2026-02-08) The lair lies at the southern end of the flooded cave. Skalanthas warned the party not to enter, and lightning-bolted Portia, who took half of 40 damage (a successful Dexterity save), when she rounded the corner.
- (2026-02-08) The monks do not go down to the lair and only Ronnom is allowed in. Locate object placed Veen's bandolier to the southeast and down, near where the lair is.

chunks.title: Dragonfjord
chunks.text:
Location: Dragonfjord (first seen 2026-02-22, last seen 2026-10-18)
Also known as: the fjord
Type: fjord
Parent: Imperium Titanicus
Description: Seen from the mountain slope on a clear, cold day: frozen blue waters, glints of ice along the shoreline, a rocky island and a ruined settlement on the eastern shore.
- The DM's map of Dragonfjord: the fjord runs south from the Sea of Storms between mountain ranges, with the Ruins of Drakholm on its eastern shore, Belurath's Fall ("beware of restless dead") to the west, and dragon lairs in the mountains on both sides, Lunae's among them. House Querid's world map places it on the Imperium's northern coast, west of Emperor's Bay.
- The DM's Dragonfjord map marks an unknown ship in the fjord with the note "Unknown ship — beware of merrows".
- (2026-02-22) The generals' planning maps did not model Dragonfjord as a landing route. Ships sailing up it could bypass the forest and the patrolled Harrowlands border and reach the plains outside Roma. The GM said it is dominated by white dragons and no one goes there.
- (2026-02-22) The hermit named at least five dragons there: Sven (oldest patriarch), Vorrel/snow mother, Rhymes scar, Sheerkess (also called cold wake) and the younger Isildrax.
- (2026-02-22) There are no roads to Dragonfjord; it can be reached by ship.
- (2026-03-08) From the camp on the Dragonfjord side the party saw a rocky island in the fjord that was not on their overland map of the empire.

chunks.title: Dragonfjord (part 2)
chunks.text:
Location: Dragonfjord (first seen 2026-02-22, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-03-08) On the eastern shore are ruins of a settlement, apparently inactive, in a natural bay with gently sloping beaches that is a good landing place for ships and rowboats. The party judged it reachable on foot in under a day. Portia saw no boats.
- (2026-03-08) The annotated map found in the wagon wreck shows five dragons, the ruins of Drakholm, restless dead and merrows, and an island with a dragon.
- (2026-03-08) The party's mission there is to find where the Norge plan to land and report it to the army; Raf thought the ruined settlement might be their landing spot.
- (2026-04-05) The party traveled down a river from the rockfall area to the shore, then north along the shore toward the ruins, using Pass without Trace for group stealth checks (34, 28 and 32 medians).
- (2026-04-05) The fjord water is frigid; within a mile of the rocky island it is colder still, and a chilly fog bank surrounds the island.
- (2026-04-05) Kyle said Dragonfjord was written off in the generals' tactical assessments despite looking like a good landing point; the party came to check it.
- (2026-04-05) The party saw a Norge longship and later several larger cargo ships beyond the island; by the next morning only the longship was visible.
- (2026-04-05) The map marks five dragons: one believed ancient, a couple adult, one younger and one uncertain.

chunks.title: Dragonfjord (part 3)
chunks.text:
Location: Dragonfjord (first seen 2026-02-22, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-04-19) The party watched the mouth of Dragonfjord for the treasure ship from a coastal camp for a day and a night and saw no ships enter. The GM said dragons range tens of miles from their lairs, so seeing one is rare.
- (2026-04-19) The GM said Dragonfjord is still within the province of Roma.
- (2026-04-19) The party's map shows five dragons, and none lie in the direction the white dragon flew off.
- (2026-05-17) A mirror-of-the-past vision showed a past battle in the fjord between a gargantuan silver dragon and a gargantuan white dragon, with Rimescar also involved and humanoid followers casting spells.
- (2026-06-14) Lunae says she was once imprisoned while fighting Icevein, who was seeking to occupy her fjord. She knew of four dragons, Icevein and three offspring. The party's map shows five, so there is one more white dragon than she knew of.
- (2026-06-14) The Norge camp on the shore holds the Fenrir's longship and now a second ship, apparently a troop transport or cargo galleon. The party thinks it carries tribute.
- (2026-07-12) The party judged that the Norge force might use Dragonfjord as a backdoor invasion route; Monarch preferred they be forced to land in a more defensible position for Roma.
- (2026-07-12) Lunae says the fjord was her neighborhood, and most of her former hoard is under the control of the ancient white dragon; she expects it to take decades to reclaim the area.

chunks.title: Dragonfjord (part 4)
chunks.text:
Location: Dragonfjord (first seen 2026-02-22, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-07-26) Icevein, an ancient white dragon from the Hvítfjall, moved into the fjord about thirty years ago; the dragons in the fjord are his offspring and are adults.
- (2026-07-26) The party traveled about eight or nine miles south from the cave to the pink star overlook, then south past the ruins of Drakholm and across a cold, chest-deep river, camping in a hidden hollow about a mile from the Cherek camp.
- (2026-07-26) A dragon similar in size to Rimescar was seen flying east to west along the river, and a smaller white dragon was seen over the mountains to the south.
- (2026-09-20) The party hid in the icy waters of the fjord at night and later sailed the Fenrir to about the middle of the fjord, a mile offshore, to rest.
- (2026-10-18) Merrows, ogre-sized, shark-featured merfolk with serrated weapons, live in the fjord waters. Three kept pace with the Fenrir at 60 ft speed but lost interest and could not climb aboard. The GM said they could have counterboarded if the ship were slower.
- (2026-10-18) The ancient white dragon Icevein was seen flying near its island and trailed the ship at about 80 ft speed (dash 160), without dashing at first. Later it dashed and overtook the ship.
- (2026-10-18) Lunae refuses to overfly the fjord in natural form because Icevein nearly killed her once. She planned to move her clan by dragon to the river mouth on the northeast side of the fjord mouth, almost 10 miles from her lair.

chunks.title: Dragonfjord (part 5)
chunks.text:
Location: Dragonfjord (first seen 2026-02-22, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-10-18) A group of creatures, possibly mounted, was seen moving south to north across the hills a couple of miles south of the party.

chunks.title: Hermit's Hut
chunks.text:
Location: Hermit's Hut (first seen 2026-02-22, last seen 2026-02-22)
Also known as: the hut
Type: hut
Parent: Foothills near Dragonfjord
Description: Hand-built stone-and-log one-room hut at the forest edge, without windows, with a poorly fitting door, a fireplace with an iron cauldron, one chair and a cot.
- (2026-02-22) The party spotted its chimney smoke, scouted inside with Monarch's clairvoyance, and spent the night there with a gray-haired hermit and his winter wolf Useless. Nothing happened overnight; Portia marked it on her map.

chunks.title: Forked Peak Pass
chunks.text:
Location: Forked Peak Pass (first seen 2026-02-22, last seen 2026-03-08)
Also known as: the pass, forked peak
Type: mountain pass
Parent: Dragonfjord
Description: Snowy mountain pass through yeti and dragon territory, with iron-bearing rock and an old cleared wagon trail.
- (2026-02-22) The party's survival checks (17 and 17) found a likely pass southwest of their landing point. The hermit warned that halfway along it drops into a bad crevasse, and that one should go up and through the two-topped forked peak instead of the apparently easy way. Yeti live higher up.
- (2026-03-08) The pass climbs more than the other route but has no ice crevasse. Its route follows the remnants of an old cleared trail wide enough for wagons, with younger trees grown back, and the rock shows signs of iron, a possible mine site.
- (2026-03-08) The party camped on the Dragonfjord side, out of the likely rockfall path and slightly upslope with sight of their approach trail. Two yeti tracked them there in the night. Portia's wall of fire killed one and Raf and Monarch killed the other.
- (2026-03-08) A group of four long-striding bipedal tracks, snowed over, diverged uphill from the party's route. Monarch suspected the yeti den in the old mine.
- (2026-03-08) Wolf howls that sounded unlike wolves were heard ahead and above, which Raf identified as yetis.

chunks.title: Dragonfjord Rubble Field
chunks.text:
Location: Dragonfjord Rubble Field (first seen 2026-03-08, last seen 2026-04-05)
Also known as: debris field, rubble field
Type: rockfall slope
Parent: Dragonfjord
Description: Long-standing snow-covered rubble field at the western foot of the mountains, from natural freeze-and-crack rockfalls.
- (2026-03-08) The rubble field at the foot of the mountains on the fjord side is a natural, regional, long-standing feature, and the party's route led through it.
- (2026-03-08) Buried in the field is a wrecked wagon of House Querid cartographers, far south of the ruined settlement, with about 10 long-dead skeletons. Salvaged items included a small gold idol worth 750 gp, jewelry worth 750 gp total, copper chalices with bone charms worth 300 gp, a court silk outfit worth 500 gp, a cartography kit, an annotated map in a scroll tube, and a sending stone. Digging it out took a big chunk of the day.
- (2026-04-05) The wagon wreck sits in the rockfall area in the lower right of the map, near one of the dragon lairs.

chunks.title: Ruins of Drakholm
chunks.text:
Location: Ruins of Drakholm (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-09-20)
Also known as: Drakholm, Drakholm ruins
Type: ruined city
Parent: Dragonfjord
Description: Collapsed stone city on the fjord's eastern shore, ringed around a central circular plaza, with a deep shore good for harboring ships.
- The DM's map labels it "Ruins of Drakholm", on the eastern shore of the Dragonfjord; the DM's picture of Drakholm shows the ruined city from above under snow, laid out in rings around a central plaza.
- (2026-04-05) The ruins are hard to spot, collapsed to foundations and hidden by snow and overgrowth; Monarch found fragments of Draconic markings and dragon-themed decorative stonework.
- (2026-04-05) Monarch estimated the stones were worked centuries ago and ruined for roughly 100 to 300 years; the buildings and steps are sized for humanoids, not dragons.
- (2026-04-05) Raf saw the city laid out in rings around a large central circular plaza, possibly an arena or ritual space; Portia noted deliberately planted tree varieties; Eddie found it an odd place for a city with no farms.
- (2026-04-05) The party sheltered the night in walled ruins under bare trees using Eddie's Tiny Hut, and nothing happened overnight.
- (2026-04-05) Monarch's history check: no known recent city here; Dragonfjord is understood as dragon country where nobody lives, though draconic civilizations exist in the western mountains.
- (2026-04-19) The Cherek camp sits north of the Ruins of Drakholm.

chunks.title: Ruins of Drakholm (part 2)
chunks.text:
Location: Ruins of Drakholm (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-09-20)
- (2026-07-26) The party passed the outskirts of Drakholm at nightfall and skirted east of it, seeing dim lights moving among the ruins that did not leave them.
- (2026-08-09) The Cherek camp the party scouted this session sits on a rocky shoreline with poor footing, with a rocky beach that clatters underfoot.
- (2026-09-20) The charmed Cherek were landed about four and a half miles north of the ship's original spot, not yet far enough to reach Drakholm, and were told to walk north there.

chunks.title: White Dragon's Island
chunks.text:
Location: White Dragon's Island (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-06-14)
Also known as: the rocky island, the island in the fjord
Type: island
Parent: Dragonfjord
Description: Rocky island a couple of miles long, rising about a thousand feet, ringed by chilly fog and ice-slick rock, with a lone rocky landing spot and trail.
- (2026-04-05) The island lies about seven miles out from the eastern shore and shows the hallmarks of an adult or ancient white dragon's lair; the party saw a huge dragon circling it from afar.
- (2026-04-05) The only landing is a small tumble of rocks with a crevice trail, anchored near by the Norge longship; no other ships were seen circling the island.
- (2026-04-05) Eddie's clairvoyance on the landing trail showed the longship pulled in, an old Goliath with a staff watching, and a masked Goliath woman wading out to the ship.
- (2026-06-14) Lunae suspects the ancient patriarch Icevein is the dragon on the island in the bay, going by the party's description.

chunks.title: Fenrir
chunks.text:
Location: Fenrir (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-10-18)
Also known as: Fenrir's, the longship, Fenrir's headed ship, Fenrir's wolf headed ship, Fenrir's Camp, the ship, Fenrir's Longship, the Fenrirs, the Fenrir, longship
Type: ship
Parent: Dragonfjord
Description: Runed Cherek longship, stolen by the party and now adrift in the bay
- (2026-04-05) It carries about 30 to 32 Cherek, mostly Goliaths, and is wrapped in dark, cold fog; approaching within 120 feet forces a wisdom save or frightened.
- (2026-04-05) Portia and Lucia failed the save and were frightened; Eddie succeeded.
- (2026-04-05) Its base speed is 50 and it cannot be clairvoyantly sensed; it rowed southeast and beached in an inlet south of the party, where the crew made camp.
- (2026-04-19) The GM said the longship is carved with many runes and has a figurehead of Fenrir, the wolf at the end of the world. The party suspects the ship itself may be the source of the Private Sanctum-like spell, since the fog is centered on it.
- (2026-04-19) The camp has one big command pavilion near the shore, behind which the ship is pulled up, and six smaller tents. It holds about 32 older Cherek warriors who look like elites, so it is more a platoon than an army. Sentries on the ship look down over the camp.
- (2026-04-19) The GM said the camp showed no signs of the dragon's attack: no collapsed tents, no frost patches and no injured people.

chunks.title: Fenrir (part 2)
chunks.text:
Location: Fenrir (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-04-19) The camp is wrapped in dark fog about 500 feet across, roughly twice the radius earlier reported. The GM said it resembles Private Sanctum upcast to 8th level: it blocks sight and sound and teleportation, and nothing blocks walking through. The fog is only obscuring from outside, and inside it is clear. Fear around the ship was reported earlier and is judged a separate effect.
- (2026-06-14) Lunae recognizes the ship as an old, old magic ship, probably sentient, and links it to the Sundered Sky clan. Scouts report wolf pelts and wolf marks at the camp, and Lunae identifies the symbols as Odin's Blind Eye, a Sundered Sky subclan serving frost giants.
- (2026-07-12) The Norge tribute convoy of three heavy wagons set out from Fenrir's camp toward the river below Rimescar's waterfalls, avoiding a route too far south toward Drakholm, and camped two thirds of the way from the shore to the planned meeting spot.
- (2026-07-26) In Lucia's mirror vision Icevein froze the sea around the Fenrir's in Dragonfjord and landed in front of it, staring at the old rune master beside Vigdis before flying off.
- (2026-07-26) The GM said the ship looks very old, like a legendary rune ship, likely an artifact; the party has no evidence it is sentient.
- (2026-07-26) Observed through Monarch's clairvoyance, only four to six crew are on deck at a time as a ready-to-move skeleton crew rather than guards, and the camp watches the sky more than the ground.

chunks.title: Fenrir (part 3)
chunks.text:
Location: Fenrir (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-07-26) The Cherek broke camp at first light and rowed the Fenrir's south along the fjord, and later a galleon dropped off a single wagon of dense cargo beside it and sailed north.
- (2026-07-26) The party planned a heist on the Fenrir's at night while Vigdis and the rune master were away delivering tribute, hoping to find hard evidence linking the Cherek to the frost giants.
- (2026-08-09) The sail is furled and stowed on deck. Its planks are carved with runes, some glowing, and a faint crackling of magical energy runs along the hull. Monarch, Portia and Eddie judged the Fenrir to behave like a magic item, and Sir Raf's natural 20 on Arcana led him to think it is an ancient artifact that obeys whoever is attuned to it.
- (2026-08-09) Two hatches lead below decks, one forward and one aft behind the bundled sail. They are watertight and latched but not locked. They appear to be warded for on-open, probably by a glyph of warding keyed to named individuals.
- (2026-08-09) Touching the ship sets it off. When Portia stepped onto the deck, a lightning bolt struck her for 33 damage, and she took 16 on her save. The wolf's head figurehead came alive and howled. The ship's frost breath is a 60-foot cone from the head that did 30 cold damage to Monarch, and Portia took 7 inside the rope coil. It cannot fire back to back. Proximity alone did not trigger it. Sir Raf's check suggested the lightning is a held chain lightning spell, and it appears to be a mode rather than always active.

chunks.title: Fenrir (part 4)
chunks.text:
Location: Fenrir (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-08-09) The wolf's head figurehead faces the shore. The bow sits about 7 or 8 feet from shore, with handholds on the hull. It stands about 25 feet from keel to gunwale, with a rowing well and roughly 10 feet of cargo space below. A full crew is about 50, including 22 oarsmen.
- (2026-08-09) The rune master's quarters are in the stern below decks, and elementals are said to be there. Vigdis Foe Shatter presumably has a cabin below decks as well.
- (2026-08-09) Two guards sat aboard: a Goliath bearsark and a Cherek hunter with a great bow. Monarch charmed both, and the Goliath bearsark then turned into a bear. They said they were afraid of the elementals and could pass through the hatches without incident.
- (2026-08-09) The party left without the documents and began planning a heist: charm the guards, have them open a hatch, and use silence, banishment and charm monster on the elementals. Monarch wants to attune to the ship, which takes an hour in contact with it and undisturbed. They decided to wait for Lucia (Andy) before attempting any of it.
- (2026-09-06) The party returned to the Cherek camp planning to charm the guards and crew aboard so they would sail the Fenrir away and steal it. Kyle ruled it can be sailed like an ordinary longship by oar and sail even by someone not attuned to it.

chunks.title: Fenrir (part 5)
chunks.text:
Location: Fenrir (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-09-06) Eddie's clairvoyance showed the guards had stayed on alert and were reinforced: three guards on the shore at the front of the ship and four on deck, a mix of giant-kin, berserkers and hunters, with the hunters on the ocean side watching the water. The figurehead rises about 10 feet above the deck.
- (2026-09-06) The ship is charged with lightning that blasts unfriendly creatures who touch it from outside. The GM said it appears to know crew from non-crew; the lightning did not reach below decks when Portia touched the interior.
- (2026-09-06) When Portia first touched the ship from inside, the figurehead awoke and howled. Eddie's Silence silenced it only while the ship stayed within the 20-foot silence sphere; once dragged out of the bubble the howl returned.
- (2026-09-06) Four charmed oarsmen hauled the ship loose of the shore. Arguing and fighting among the crew then left it at a standstill, with the sail up and the hunter at the rudder.
- (2026-09-20) The ship pulled away from shore under one or two pairs of oars while Cherek crew brawled on deck, and it crackled with lightning. Lucia and Sir Raf swam out to it at night and boarded via the open hatch.
- (2026-09-20) Sir Raf failed to beat the chain lightning on touching the hull (18 save, not high enough for a legendary vessel). He took 39 lightning, halved to 19 by the borrowed ring of lightning resistance.

chunks.title: Fenrir (part 6)
chunks.text:
Location: Fenrir (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-09-20) Once the ship left the bubble of silence the wolf-head's howl returned, and the frost breath originates at the head while the lightning crackles along the entire hull. The ship distinguishes crew from enemies.
- (2026-09-20) The two hatch wards are independent glyphs of warding set to trigger when the hatches close. Eddie's dispel magic removed them with the other third-level spells.
- (2026-09-20) Portia attuned to the Fenrir after an hour while Monarch kept the charmed Cherek in agreement; the party were then designated crew, and the lightning hull and frost breath can be switched on or off. Portia turned the lightning and howl off to hide the ship.
- (2026-09-20) The party sailed the ship, with Sir Raf steering and Eddie and Lucia on the sails (group check middle roll 18), out to about a mile offshore in the dark. The sail was lowered into a pile and the anchor found no bottom.
- (2026-09-20) Eddie cast dispel magic on the Fenrir during the long rest; the obscuring mist and some other spells ended but the persistent fear aura stayed.
- (2026-10-04) The boarding ward is a single toggle: if on, the ship activates its howl and chain lightning blast itself against boarders; if off, they can only be triggered manually. Portia had switched off the lightning and howling so the ship would not be a beacon in the water.
- (2026-10-04) The longship has no longboat or life raft; it is designed to go to shore by itself.

chunks.title: Fenrir (part 7)
chunks.text:
Location: Fenrir (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-10-04) Per the ship's movement rules, an air elemental guarantees maximum favorable wind (+60 ft movement) and a water elemental guarantees maximum current (+60 ft); both together give 120 ft speed with no crew. Navigation is a Survival check; steering is a Strength check.
- (2026-10-04) Raising the sail is a two-person job needing a Strength check and a Dexterity check without proficiency; Eddie rolled it and the sail was left in a passable but untidy state, ready to raise. The party left the sails down so the ship stays low and hard to spot.
- (2026-10-04) With Monarch's air elemental summoned and her attuning to the water stone, the party got underway powered by elementals, heading north-northwest toward White Crown.
- (2026-10-04) The captain's cabin's contents were left in place; whatever is under the bearskin was left untouched until the ship reaches safe harbor.
- (2026-10-04) Azuriel replied that the Fenrir is a critical asset: return it to Roma or destroy it at all costs.
- (2026-10-18) The GM said the Fenrir is highly recognizable, so there is no mystery about what ship it is the moment anyone sees it.
- (2026-10-18) The party dispelled nothing: Eddie rolled 10 plus guidance (needed 18-19) and Portia also failed, so the persistent fear effect on the ship remains. Raf and Monarch identified it as antipathy/sympathy, an eighth-level spell that normally affects only huge-size or smaller targets, so it has been modified, possibly by a wish, a rune or group casting.

chunks.title: Fenrir (part 8)
chunks.text:
Location: Fenrir (first seen 2026-04-05, last seen 2026-10-18)
- (2026-10-18) The hull is covered in thousands of weathered runes, many below the waterline. The GM said deciphering them would take days.
- (2026-10-18) Speed rules from the GM: a water elemental gives 60 ft, and sails up with an elemental give 120 ft (12 mph). 24 oarsmen plus two elementals gave 24 mph. The ship has benches for 24 rowers, and its crew complement is 40.
- (2026-10-18) The GM ruled the Fenrir can carry the party plus 40 dwarves. The party planned to keep them out of the forward cabin because of the bearskin-covered object.
- (2026-10-18) Fenrir's defenses were switched on during the dragon chase (lightning boarding ward, howl and winter's blast). Portia decided on them. They were turned off at 02:10, and before facing the imperial spell jammers she kept only the lightning boarding ward.
- (2026-10-18) The party sailed it north along Dragonfjord's east side, ran the Norge blockade into Emperor's Bay with sails changed by permanent major image to Roman colors, and was targeted by two imperial spell jammers' ballistas.
- (2026-10-18) A message from Lunae said she would observe as an eagle. Later she landed aboard, in Elven form, while the ship was racing through Emperor's Bay.

chunks.title: Rimescar's lair
chunks.text:
Location: Rimescar's lair (first seen 2026-04-19, last seen 2026-07-12)
Type: dragon lair
Parent: Dragonfjord
Description: Lair of the white dragon Rimescar, in flooded mining caverns whose floors are frozen river ice, with open water by the walls.
- (2026-04-19) The dead dwarf, questioned with Speak with Dead, answered that his group came from and escaped from Rimescar, and that 25 others are still there. Rimescar is one of the five dragon names on the party's map.
- (2026-04-19) The dwarves dug tunnels to escape, and the dragon's hoard is within. The party tracked the dwarves' trail toward where the map shows a dragon.
- (2026-05-17) The Mithril Peaks dwarves are confined to a corner of the cave system. The dragon rests on the other side of the frozen river, about 50 or 60 feet beyond where the party met the dwarves; the dwarves said to follow the left-hand wall of the tunnel to reach it.
- (2026-05-17) The lair was originally a Mithril Peaks mine, useful for its flowing water. Rimescar took it over and forces the dwarves to mine mithril for him.
- (2026-05-17) The caves are flooded, and the floors exist because the river was frozen by the dragon's breath, though not all of the water is frozen. Water flows under the ice and out through a waterfall.
- (2026-05-17) Clairvoyance showed a big open cavern with an ice-covered floor and ice-coated walls. A pile of herbivore carcasses was there and yeti fed on them while Rimescar watched. No treasure was visible.

chunks.title: Rimescar's lair (part 2)
chunks.text:
Location: Rimescar's lair (first seen 2026-04-19, last seen 2026-07-12)
- (2026-05-17) Rimescar slipped into the water, swam upstream under the ice and was lost from sight. He later burst out through the waterfall to the outside, and a dwarf reply told the party they would have an hour.
- (2026-05-17) A Locate Object cast for the iron flask said it is within 1,000 feet, up and to the east of the party.
- (2026-06-14) Portia's fireball melted the ice surface in a 20-foot-radius circle, leaving water over ice, and sent a tremor through the ice. The dwarves shouted 'no fire, you fools, you'll summon it, and we don't mean the dragon'.
- (2026-06-14) The dwarves murmured to Eddie that a creature lives in the ice and hunts on heat. It is far off because no fire has been used in weeks. If it comes, it is almost as dangerous as the dragon.
- (2026-06-14) Portia's nature check narrowed the heat-hunter to a frost salamander or a remorhaz, probably the salamander. Lunae later agreed it was most likely a frost salamander, which can sense heat from farther away the hotter the source and can be bargained with.
- (2026-06-14) The pool in the lower right of the lair map is the top of a waterfall where underground river water exits the mountain, which is why it never freezes. The walls are ice-covered stone.
- (2026-06-14) Locate object pointed to a section of very thick ice beside Eddie. Sir Raf, enlarged by Monarch, smashed through 15 feet of it with Shatterspike in about a minute, 150 hit points of wall.

chunks.title: Rimescar's lair (part 3)
chunks.text:
Location: Rimescar's lair (first seen 2026-04-19, last seen 2026-07-12)
- (2026-06-14) Behind the ice was a hollowed stone chamber, the dragon's hoard room, holding about 100,000 coins (mostly silver, some gold and platinum), mithril bars, a cracked dragon egg, a jeweled glove, an iron flask, a scroll case and a living-wood staff. Three living cold breaths guarded it. The party took the flask and the other items plus handfuls of coin, and Monarch cast a fourth-level major image of the intact ice wall behind them.
- (2026-06-14) Rimescar returned carrying yeti, burst up through the water by the waterfall, and breathed cold on Lunae in dwarf form. Lunae, immune to cold, breathed paralyzing breath back, burning through his legendary resistances. The dwarves' crossbows killed him while he was paralyzed. Lunae's clan means to eat him.
- (2026-07-12) Rimescar's lair has two entrances the party uses: a hidden tunnel at the back bottom of the hill and the waterfall; the dragon's own main way in and out is swimming up the waterfall, which no wagon could manage.
- (2026-07-12) The party planned to stage the tribute meeting by the lair while keeping the Norge delegation from entering it, since a dragon has lair advantages that make negotiating inside undesirable.

chunks.title: Dwarf Escape Crevice and Lair Tunnel
names: Dwarf Escape Crevice and Lair Tunnel
chunks.text:
Location: Dwarf Escape Crevice and Lair Tunnel (first seen 2026-04-19, last seen 2026-05-17)
Also known as: the crevice, frozen waterfall crevice
Type: cave passage
Parent: Dragonfjord
Description: Natural crevice beside frozen waterfalls leading into the dragon's lair, dug into by dwarves
- (2026-04-19) The party followed the dwarves' trail to a narrow natural crevice beside a frozen waterfall, partway up a mountain. The frozen falls are unnaturally frozen, and the area grew extremely cold near the dragon's lair.
- (2026-04-19) The crevice narrows until even Monarch must squeeze. A dwarven mining tunnel enters from the side, with rubble stuffed back into the crevice. It climbs steeply as a five-foot passage and then a vertical shaft of about 60 feet with carved handholds, widening to 10 feet across. The surface above is all ice. The party's group stealth check was 21.
- (2026-04-19) At the top, two ice trolls attacked the party in the hallway, and a dragon's roar echoed from further in.
- (2026-05-17) The party fought two ice trolls at the top of the shaft and dragged the corpses to the intersection. The shaft leads back outside and is too narrow for the dragon to fit through.
- (2026-05-17) Near the bottom of the shaft are crawlspace tunnels too small for the dragon. They open into low dwarf-height mining tunnels where the party rested and took a long rest.
- (2026-05-17) The mining tunnels show glints of mithril ore and a little silver dust, but have been mined out.

chunks.title: Dwarf Escape Crevice and Lair Tunnel (part 2)
names: Dwarf Escape Crevice and Lair Tunnel
chunks.text:
Location: Dwarf Escape Crevice and Lair Tunnel (first seen 2026-04-19, last seen 2026-05-17)
- (2026-05-17) Monarch cast a permanent fourth-level illusion over the hole so the corridor looks like a dead end, and the GM warned the dragon would notice someone had done it. The party also heard growling that sounded like language not spoken by any of them.

chunks.title: Astral Library of the Silver Dragon
names: Astral Library of the Silver Dragon
chunks.text:
Location: Astral Library of the Silver Dragon (first seen 2026-04-19, last seen 2026-06-14)
Also known as: astral library
Type: astral plane library
Parent: Astral Plane
Description: Library of endless stacks of books and scrolls, with spirits of heroes, scholars and dangerous creatures
- (2026-04-19) During the roar, Monarch, Portia and Lucia were pulled onto the Astral Plane, where a silver dragon spirit said she was only somewhat trapped and opened a door into a vast library. She said the party would have all the time they needed but perhaps not all the safety they wished.
- (2026-05-17) Monarch, Portia and Lucia were taken to the library with three other adventuring groups, and each person could ask one question.
- (2026-05-17) The library has sections for past, present and future. Monarch went off to the future section with a fungal dwarf, and the library held people from many times and planes. Dragon cult members wander there too.
- (2026-05-17) Portia's question returned that the silver dragon Lunae languishes in a legendary iron flask buried behind thick ice in Rimescar's hoard.
- (2026-05-17) Monarch learned that the dragon masks are destroyed when an ancient dragon willingly casts wish to destroy it, and that only two masks are needed to free Tiamat.
- (2026-06-14) Monarch described to Lunae the future-section knowledge that an ancient white dragon will cast wish to destroy the dragon masks.

chunks.title: Duchy of Maulring
chunks.text:
Location: Duchy of Maulring (first seen 2026-05-17, last seen 2026-07-26)
Also known as: Maulring, Mawring
Type: principality
Description: Small independent principality in the mountains between the Kingdom of the West and the Imperium, devoted almost entirely to dragon hunting. It is said to place the spirits of fallen soldiers in Warforged.
- (2026-05-17) Lucia rolled a 20 on history and recognized the armored riders pursuing a wounded Rimescar in the mirror vision as Maulringers from the Duchy of Maulring.
- (2026-07-12) Maulring lies west of Dragonfjord; its society opposes all dragonkind, and its dragon slayers bear marks, shown as dragon skulls below the collarbone, for each dragon slaying they took part in. Maulring pioneered or rediscovered the creation of Warforged.
- (2026-07-26) The GM said Maulringers are only unreasonable about dragons within the Duchy of Maulring and are pragmatic outside it.

chunks.title: Rimescar's Waterfall Pool and Staging Area
names: Rimescar's Waterfall Pool and Staging Area
chunks.text:
Location: Rimescar's Waterfall Pool and Staging Area (first seen 2026-07-12, last seen 2026-07-12)
Also known as: the waterfall pool, the meeting spot
Type: river pool and meeting ground
Parent: Dragonfjord
Description: A pool below Rimescar's lair, screened by rock outcroppings so it cannot be seen from the lowlands; the river there runs through steep falls too narrow for wagons. Monarch placed her permanent Major Image of Rimescar there and an illusory snow-covered mound as a hidey hole for the party. The tribute exchange took place in the open ground marked by the purple arrow on the map.
- (2026-07-12) Monarch cast Major Image at fourth level, making it permanent, in a pool hidden by rock outcroppings; Portia helped pick the spot.
- (2026-07-12) The steep waterfall section is unsuitable for wagons; the meeting happened in open ground before the convoy reached the river.

chunks.title: Hvítfjall
chunks.text:
Location: Hvítfjall (first seen 2026-07-26, last seen 2026-07-26)
Also known as: Great White Mountain, the White Mountain
Type: mountain
Parent: Norge
Description: The Great White Mountain of Norge, formerly the lair of the ancient white dragon Icevein, far outside the clans' realm.
- Hvítfjall, the White Mountain in Norge.
- (2026-07-26) Sorcha said the ancient white dragon Icevein is lord of Hvítfjall, the Great White Mountain in Norge.
- (2026-07-26) The GM said Hvítfjall lies well outside the realm of the Cherek clans, in a frozen wasteland.

chunks.title: Norge
chunks.text:
Location: Norge (first seen 2026-07-26, last seen 2026-07-26)
Also known as: Nord
Type: region
Description: Northern realm of the Cherek, across the Sea of Storms from the Imperium.
- On House Querid's map Norge lies north of the Imperium across the Sea of Storms.
- (2026-07-26) About thirty years ago the great Jarl consolidated power over the clans, which reduced internal raids and increased raids on the Imperium; the frost giants consolidated soon after.
- (2026-07-26) Sorcha reported a Norge fleet of hundreds of ships carrying tens of thousands, about five times the largest estimate in the frost giants' planning rooms.

chunks.title: Cherek Camp Pavilion
chunks.text:
Location: Cherek Camp Pavilion (first seen 2026-08-09, last seen 2026-08-09)
Also known as: leader's tent, main tent, command tent, pavilion
Type: tent
Parent: Fenrir
Description: Large central tent of the Cherek camp, with satellite camps and watch fires spread around it.
- (2026-08-09) The camp is spread out to avoid breath weapons, with a main camp and satellite camps, one person at each watch fire, and a couple of people aboard the ship.
- (2026-08-09) The scrying sensor did not appear, and Sir Raf deduced the pavilion is under private sanctum, a fourth-level abjuration that blocks scrying. Detect magic found abjuration inside the tent.
- (2026-08-09) Raf silently lifted a stake and the party looked inside. Four bedrolls were occupied: a bearsark, a berserker, a Goliath, and a commander sleeping in armor on a separate bedroll trimmed with many furs. Portia as a spider searched the commander's pack and bedroll and found no documents.

chunks.title: Fenrir Below Decks
chunks.text:
Location: Fenrir Below Decks (first seen 2026-09-06, last seen 2026-09-20)
Also known as: below decks, the hold
Type: ship interior
Parent: Fenrir
Description: Compartmentalized hold, about 10 feet high, entered by a hatch and ladder.
- (2026-09-06) The hold has three compartments divided by bulkheads. The large center compartment is a galley and sleeping area with hammocks, two small tables with stools and the mast in the middle. The forward and rear compartments each have two doors, and a bilge lies below a floor.
- (2026-09-06) Two doors were guarded by a bearsark and a Goliath bearsark, and a Goliath lounged in a hammock. A third crewman was in the center compartment.
- (2026-09-06) Portia opened a door and saw huge glowing rune stones holding elemental energy, a fine hammock and a very fine chest. A tall figure in black plate with flame showing through the cracks rose out of the runes, and she shut the door again.
- (2026-09-20) Below decks has hammocks, a long table and stools for the galley, doors in the bulkheads and steps up to the other hatch. Two crew cabins were checked and found to be empty of rations and personal effects, with a latch but no lock.
- (2026-09-20) Four rune-carved stones stand in one cabin; the party found two glowing after dispel magic, and opening the door brought forth an armored fire elemental and an invisible air elemental.

chunks.title: Rune Stone Cabin of the Fenrir
names: Rune Stone Cabin of the Fenrir
chunks.text:
Location: Rune Stone Cabin of the Fenrir (first seen 2026-09-20, last seen 2026-10-04)
Also known as: rune master's quarters, room with the rune stones
Type: ship cabin
Parent: Fenrir Below Decks
Description: Cabin with a hammock, four giant runed stones tied to fire, air, ice and water, and an empty footlocker.
- (2026-09-20) The four stones link to elemental planes; attuned and fed a spell slot, each calls an elemental bound to the stone and the user. The rear stone summons an armored fire elemental, the forward one an air elemental, with water and ice elementals presumed for the others. Elementals near the stones have advantage on saves against spells.
- (2026-09-20) Portia's charm monster pacified the fire elemental, and Monarch's charm monster pacified the air elemental after Portia's attempt failed; the GM ended the fight with both friendly. The footlocker is unlocked, unwarded and empty.
- (2026-10-04) The party's dispel magic had ended two of the four stones' spells, so only two elementals appeared; Portia and Monarch each charmed one after the long rest.
- (2026-10-04) The party attuned to the fire and air stones over an hour. Charm lasted one hour. The GM ruled an attuned stone, with a fourth-level slot, summons an elemental until killed or dismissed. If someone else attunes the stone the elemental is dismissed. The air stone calls an air elemental or invisible stalker; the fire stone a fire elemental or fire elemental myrmidon.

chunks.title: Rune Stone Cabin of the Fenrir (part 2)
names: Rune Stone Cabin of the Fenrir
chunks.text:
Location: Rune Stone Cabin of the Fenrir (first seen 2026-09-20, last seen 2026-10-04)
- (2026-10-04) Monarch attuned the air (wind) stone and summoned an air elemental to guard the deck while she attuned the water stone; Eddie planned to attune the water stone and Sir Raf attuned the air stone briefly before switching back to Shatterspike.

chunks.title: Vigdis's Captain's Cabin on the Fenrir
names: Vigdis's Captain's Cabin on the Fenrir
chunks.text:
Location: Vigdis's Captain's Cabin on the Fenrir (first seen 2026-10-04, last seen 2026-10-04)
Also known as: captain's quarters, last guarded cabin
Type: ship cabin
Parent: Fenrir Below Decks
Description: Small cabin with a meeting table, hammock, a trapped locked trunk and a bearskin-covered large flat object
- (2026-10-04) Its door lock was decent (about DC 20) but untrapped; Lucia picked it with ease.
- (2026-10-04) The trunk's lock triggers a trap if picked or forced; Lucia disarmed it with a Sleight of Hand total of 40, with Eddie's guidance and Hades' aid, revealing a piston that smashes hammerheads onto a gem. The gem was a warm evocation fire gem; the chest is lined with magnesium-infused wood meant to burn everything inside.
- (2026-10-04) The trunk held letters and logbooks addressed to Vigdis, showing an invasion fleet from Norge of tens of thousands focused on Roma, ordered by 'the winter favored', with communications with the clans restricted by 'the terms'. It also held 1,000 platinum, 5,000 gold and 20 trade gems worth 100 gp each (17,000 gp total), which Lucia took into her bag of holding.
- (2026-10-04) The large flat object against the back wall is covered with a bearskin and reads as divination and conjuration magic; it was left covered.

chunks.title: Houndsgate Bridge
chunks.text:
Location: Houndsgate Bridge (first seen 2024-10-20, last seen 2024-10-20)
Type: bridge
Parent: Roma
Description: Bridge where an earlier set of assassins was told to go for payment.
- Houndsgate is one of the gates of Corona Domini, on its south-east side, where a bridge crosses the Canalis Ambiente (DM's map).
- (2024-10-20) Assassins sent after Lyra were told to go to Houndsgate Bridge for payment, with no stated time or day. The party's two long rests since then mean Valkrath likely knows they failed.

chunks.title: Edgewood
chunks.text:
Location: Edgewood (first seen ?, last seen ?)
- Dansi of Edgewood, the wildshaping druid, takes their name from it.

chunks.title: Hither
chunks.text:
Location: Hither (first seen ?, last seen ?)
Type: domain
Parent: Feywild
- A place in the Feywild; the unicorn Lamorna arrived from it and returned to it.

chunks.title: Charnel Candle
chunks.text:
Item: Charnel Candle (first seen 2024-10-20, last seen 2024-11-03)
Type: candle
Holder: Monarch
Properties: Burns with a sickly dim yellow flame like a grease fire; in its light invisible skulks appear as dim translucent forms that are hard to see but not invisible.
Significance: Used to reveal the invisible skulks in the room
- (2024-11-03) Monarch took out her last candle, which smelled worse than it looked, and set it in the middle of the table after Fickle's silent warning about invisible skulks.
- (2024-11-03) Monarch grabbed the candle and lit it with Druidcraft; a skulk entering its light was revealed and became visible.
- (2024-11-03) The GM ruled that throwing the candle into the fire would not work, because the candle's own light is what makes the skulks visible.
- (2024-11-03) Monarch burned a visible skulk to ash with Fire Bolt in the candle's flames; its light also lit the skulk Thor shot dead.
- (2024-10-20) Monarch pulled out the one charnel candle as a free interact and lit it with the Druidcraft cantrip.
- (2024-10-20) In the candle's light the invisible skulks appeared as dim translucent forms, still difficult to see but not invisible.
- (2024-10-20) Monarch formed a fire bolt from the candle's flame as special effects; the flame was a sickly dim yellow like a grease fire.
- (2024-10-20) Monarch set the candle on the ground as a free object interaction, leaving it there.
- (2024-10-20) Monarch has one more candle left and let it burn through the short rest; Lyra also has one Monarch gave her.

chunks.title: Drow Poison
chunks.text:
Item: Drow Poison (first seen 2024-10-20, last seen 2024-11-03)
Also known as: drow sleep poison, drow poison injury
Type: poison (injury)
Holder: Eddie
Properties: DC 13 Constitution save; on a failure the target is poisoned for an hour, and if it fails by 5 or more it is unconscious for that hour with no shaking it off. One vial coats six projectiles or one melee weapon, only piercing or slashing; evaporates within a minute of application. Applying takes an object interaction to draw and an action to apply. Brewed only in darkness; effective in sunlight. Typically 200 gp each on the shadow market.
Significance: Drow assassins used it on Lucia and Portia, knocking both unconscious; the party looted four vials
- (2024-11-03) Eddie prepared the drow sleep poison for the ambush, asking about dunking arrows one at a time. The GM said it dries out within a minute and a bonus action normally dunks all six.
- (2024-11-03) Eddie dunked two arrows with a bonus action and shot Valkrath with one for 6 damage. The poison was moot because the arrow killed him.
- (2024-10-20) Lucia and Portia each failed their Constitution save by 5 or more against the poison from hand crossbow bolts and fell unconscious; Lucia's roll was a 6 and Portia's an 8.
- (2024-10-20) The GM said it is classic drow sleep poison with no known antidote; the amount was small and would wear off in about an hour.
- (2024-10-20) The party took four vials from the four dead drow assassins, worth 200 gp each (800 gp).

chunks.title: Drow Poison (part 2)
chunks.text:
Item: Drow Poison (first seen 2024-10-20, last seen 2024-11-03)

- (2024-10-20) The poison saves at DC 13 Constitution; failure means poisoned for an hour, and failure by 5 or more means unconscious for the hour.

chunks.title: Staff of Shield (unspelled staff) (part 2)

chunks.title: Dragon Masks
chunks.text:
Item: Dragon Masks (first seen 2024-11-17, last seen 2026-07-12)
Also known as: legendary blue dragon mask, blue dragon mask, dragon mask
Type: legendary artifact (blue dragon mask)
Significance: Wearing a dragon mask gives credibility with dragons of its color; the Cherek hold a white dragon mask the party wants.
Holder: Monarch
Properties: Advantage on skills against blue dragons; adds Charisma bonus to AC when unarmored (Monarch: plus five AC); one legendary resistance per day; lingering shock/lightning immunity benefit; grants Draconic speech. Wearing it is required to use it.
Magic: Identify (cast by Sir Raf) showed a legendary artifact deeply tied to blue dragons; wearing it requires attunement. Identify does not reveal curses or hidden effects.
- (2024-11-17) Legend says there is one dragon mask per dragon type; a wearer can speak with dragons and has significant influence, not charm or domination.
- (2024-11-17) Rumors say gathering several metallic or chromatic masks could summon Bahamut or Tiamat.
- (2025-05-18) Eddie said the party is looking for a mask, likely deep under the city; Eddie planned Locate Object using his drawing of it, range 1,000 feet.
- (2025-05-18) A mural in the Tower of Storms basement showed giants forging five masks as keys to Tiamat's prison and giving them to devils; one mask was later handed back by a succubus-like devil and placed with an amorphous gargantuan monstrosity imprisoned deep under the city.

chunks.title: Dragon Masks (part 2)
chunks.text:
Item: Dragon Masks (first seen 2024-11-17, last seen 2026-07-12)
- (2025-05-18) A captured fanatic's notes say clues to the dragon mask's location should be in the Tower of Storms basement; she did not think the mask itself was there.
- (2025-06-15) The Cult of the Dragon believes the masks are the keys to Tiamat's prison; the party had worked out earlier that the cultists were looking for the same mask.
- (2025-06-15) The Giant's research books confirm the masks were part of the binding that holds Tiamat in her prison, so they are keys to freeing her; sources differ on whether a couple or all five are needed.
- (2025-06-15) A blue dragon mask gives tremendous influence over blue dragons; scholars split between finding the masks to secure them and leaving them buried.
- (2025-06-15) The captive devil in the chest said some masks are missing, stolen perhaps by one like him, but not by him.
- (2025-06-15) The party has only seen the one drawing, which looks like a blue dragon; the GM said Tiamat's scales are large enough to make a mask from one.
- (2025-07-27) Arcana study suggested the Dragon Mask works in the prison as a source of power, since it has no giant magic; removing it could badly weaken the prison unless a similar-power item replaced it.
- (2025-07-27) The party decided to seek another legendary item as a replacement rather than simply taking the mask.

chunks.title: Dragon Masks (part 3)
chunks.text:
Item: Dragon Masks (first seen 2024-11-17, last seen 2026-07-12)
- (2025-10-19) The party saw the blue dragon scale mask floating on the undulating ooze at the center of a rune web, 30 feet from the pit's edge, ringed by ten colossal dragon statues. The Dreamcaster's notes show he knew it lay beneath Qul'drik but not that it was part of anything else.
- (2025-11-02) Monarch pulled the mask out of the rune web after Black Razor was installed, then she opened her Bag of Holding so Raf could drop the mask inside.
- (2025-11-02) The GM said the mask whispered 'it's yours by right' to Eddie as the mask was removed.
- (2025-11-02) Sir Raf cast Identify on the mask using a 100 gp pearl, which is not consumed but must be owned. The GM listed its properties.
- (2025-11-02) The mask is glossy azure with spikes around the edges, not subtle, and big enough to fit over a dragonborn's head.
- (2025-11-02) The party agreed not to wear it around town because nations would come after it. They kept it in a bag of holding for deep storage, and Eddie has not decided what to do with it.
- (2026-04-05) The GM said the party's masks give advantage on negotiating with dragons rather than commanding them. The Cherek goliath woman wore a stylized white dragon mask similar to theirs; the party wanted to remove it and withheld the mask detail from the Imperium message.

chunks.title: Dragon Masks (part 4)
chunks.text:
Item: Dragon Masks (first seen 2024-11-17, last seen 2026-07-12)
- (2026-04-19) Kyle said the attuned, identified blue dragon mask does not control blue dragons. It gives advantage on Charisma checks for interactions with them and lets the wearer speak Draconic. Other masks may differ, and chromatic dragons may respect the mask's link to Tiamat.
- (2026-05-17) Monarch learned in the astral library that the masks are used in a ritual to break Tiamat from her planar prison and that many groups seek them. Each mask is destroyed when an ancient dragon of its color willingly casts wish; only two masks are needed to free Tiamat.
- (2026-05-17) No other group knows where the blue mask is. The party knows where the white one is. The blue mask is in a bag of holding, and the party agreed Eddie should carry it.
- (2026-06-14) Monarch told Lunae the masks are used by the Cult of the Dragon to free Tiamat, and that destroying one requires an ancient dragon of its color to willingly wish it destroyed; the Norge have the white mask. Eddie was asked to mark the blue mask as his in the party inventory.
- (2026-06-14) Lunae warned most chromatic dragons would not make the wish since Tiamat's return would strengthen them, and suggested a dragon from another time.
- (2026-07-12) Eddie attuned to the blue dragon mask to learn how it works, and learned that the mask grants the ability to speak Draconic.
- (2026-07-12) Kyle explained that a dragon of the mask's color recognizes the mask's essence and respects it; there is no visual fanfare, it works like a badge of office.

chunks.title: Dragon Masks (part 5)
chunks.text:
Item: Dragon Masks (first seen 2024-11-17, last seen 2026-07-12)
- (2026-07-12) Monarch attuned to the blue dragon mask (unattuning from another item, which she judged to be worth two AC), taking it out of the party inventory; Eddie unequipped it. Holder is now Monarch.
- (2026-07-12) Monarch noted the mask grants legendary resistance once per day and that it is better than her bracers of defense.

chunks.title: Scroll of Daylight

- (2024-12-15) Monarch said she wanted to buy a scroll of daylight (a third-level spell, uncommon consumable) as a backup plan to turn on the lights in the magical darkness of Bay 3.
- (2024-12-15) Kyle ruled the scroll costs 300 gp (a spell scroll's value is double its scribing cost: 150 gp doubled). Monarch agreed to pay 300 gp from her own funds.
- (2024-12-15) Monarch noted that casting a scroll of a spell above her normal level needs a check and that a failure consumes the spell. She has several ways to gain advantage on such checks.
- (2025-02-16) At the Stormgale clan camp Monarch offered the Scroll of Daylight (market value 300 gp) in barter; Kyle ruled a 10% barter discount, so it counts as 270 gp toward the scrolls she wants, and the clan gives no change.
- (2025-02-16) Monarch planned to swap it for two first-level scrolls, Comprehend Languages and Detect Magic, valued at 50 gp each.
- (2025-02-16) Not held at the end of the session: "Yeah. Daylight's a third level spell. Yes. I didn't have any trouble finding those two scrolls. Right?" (Monarch)
- (2025-03-02) Monarch used a scroll of mage armor she had made, lasting eight hours, to cover the dinner.

- (2024-12-15) Monarch bought a hooded lantern because she has no darkvision or other extra senses and relies on her own eyes.
- (2024-12-15) On the swing shift Monarch carried the lantern lit but covered while flying her patrol route.

chunks.title: Kyber Shard
chunks.text:
Item: Kyber Shard (first seen 2024-12-15, last seen 2025-01-05)
Also known as: kyber crystal, kyber dragon shard, dragon shard, Siberys shard
Type: dragon shard (crystal)
Properties: Monarch's research says a large, whole shard is needed to bind an elemental into the ring of an Eberron-style airship. Such shards are illegal to export, like a controlled substance.
Significance: Kyber shards bind spirits and elementals into machines; they stay useful only when whole. The Sentry's destroyed fragments are no longer usable.
- (2024-12-15) Monarch concluded that the ring-shaped ship being built matches images of Eberron airships. Dragon shards, probably a kyber shard, bind the elemental that powers the ring. Kyle confirmed this was what she had learned.
- (2024-12-15) Monarch said the box had anti-scrying protection and was probably lead lined, so its contents would be invisible to Locate Object. The party hoped the shard had been removed from the box.
- (2024-12-15) Portia cast Locate Object for a kyber crystal and sensed one stationary within Shimmerstone Shipworks. Triangulation by Portia and Eddie (with Raf's help) narrowed it to Bay 3, the pit.
- (2024-12-15) Through Diego's senses, Raf saw two crystalline shapes side by side in a container the same size and shape as the delivered box. The great Zulk told Serge to bring the smaller, darker one rather than the larger one, and Serge began working with it.

chunks.title: Kyber Shard (part 2)
chunks.text:
Item: Kyber Shard (first seen 2024-12-15, last seen 2025-01-05)
- (2025-01-05) Fragments of a blue-violet crystal were found among the wreckage of the Sentry. Kyle said the color suggests a Kyber shard, used to bind spirits and tied to the nether planes. Raf and Eddie noticed the fragments with passive perception 18 and 15.
- (2025-01-05) The shard had to stay whole to function; the fragments can serve only as evidence and no one can claim to have a Kyber shard.
- (2025-01-05) Kyle clarified the party was tracking a Saberus shard, the larger and rarer kind used to build eldritch machines. Kyber shards bind elementals into them. The crystal in the Sentry is unconfirmed as Kyber.
- (2025-01-05) Monarch told Azuriel they believe the package held a Saberus dragon shard, used to build an elemental-bound airship.
- (2025-01-05) The party keeps the fragments in the party stash on the Miro board.

chunks.title: Jar of the Great Zulk
chunks.text:
Item: Jar of the Great Zulk (first seen 2024-12-15, last seen 2024-12-15)
Also known as: glass vessel, great Zulk's jar
Type: glass jar / vessel
Properties: A glass vessel from which a whiny, needly voice issues orders. The voice claims to be the great Zulk.
Significance: Holds the voice that co-directs the Bay 3 work with the work chief Wizen.
- (2024-12-15) Raf, through Diego, located the whiny voice as coming from a glass jar. Its occupant called itself the great Zulk, shouting 'I command you as the great zulk' while directing Serge.

chunks.title: Sentry Armor Plates
chunks.text:
Item: Sentry Armor Plates (first seen 2025-01-05, last seen 2025-01-05)
Also known as: armor plates from the Sentry
Type: salvage / crafting materials
Significance: Worth 500 gp toward crafting plate mail, or 250 gp if sold
- (2025-01-05) The destroyed Sentry was made of high-quality armor plates, usable for plate mail.
- (2025-01-05) Kyle valued the plates at 500 gp toward crafting plate mail, or 250 gp if sold. Raf has heavy armor proficiency.
- (2025-01-05) The party decided to keep the plates in the party stash for now.

chunks.title: Trade Bars
chunks.text:
Item: Trade Bars (first seen 2025-01-05, last seen 2026-02-22)
Also known as: laundered trade bars
Type: payment / currency
Significance: Part of the 2,500 gp reward from Merrill, paid in 100 gp platinum trade bars and gems
- (2025-01-05) A few days later at the Golden Leaf, Jimmy Slips delivered laundered trade bars instead of the stolen goods, so no locate object can trace them.
- (2025-01-05) The take was 8,000 gold; 30% is 2,400 gold, split five ways at 480 each.
- (2026-02-22) The reward was 2,500 gold in 100 gp platinum trade bars and 100 gp gems. Monarch pooled it with the 5,000 gp bounty and the trade gems, and the total came to 3,000 gold each.

chunks.title: Magic Rapier
chunks.text:
Item: Magic Rapier (first seen 2025-01-05, last seen 2025-01-05)
Also known as: plus one rapier
Type: magic weapon
Significance: Planned purchase for Sir Raf's melee
- (2025-01-05) Raf said he will look for a magic rapier as his primary melee weapon. Kyle said a magic version of a Player's Handbook weapon costs 400 gp plus the item cost. Monarch said she had added the rapier to the cards.

chunks.title: Letter from Sir Saravar
chunks.text:
Item: Letter from Sir Saravar (first seen 2025-01-19, last seen 2025-01-19)
Also known as: letter vouching for Raf
Type: document
Holder: Sir Raf
Properties: Vouches for Raf to any imperial military units near the Dawnrealm border; may deter or ease conscription, and could lead to a higher rank.
Significance: Protection against conscription and suspicion of spying near Sun Dragon.
- (2025-01-19) Sir Raf was able to obtain a letter from Sir Saravar vouching for him to any imperial military units in the area; Kyle told Jim to add it to his sheet.
- (2025-01-19) Kyle ruled the letter cuts two ways: the army may not want to anger Sir Saravar by conscripting Raf, or may make him an officer at higher pay. Raf is wary of letting others know about it.

chunks.title: Quiver of Ehlonna
chunks.text:
Item: Quiver of Ehlonna (first seen 2025-01-19, last seen 2026-09-20)
Type: uncommon magic item (quiver)
Holder: Eddie
Properties: Quiver.
Significance: Bought by Eddie in preparation for the Xi'an Palace job.
- (2025-01-19) Eddie bought a Quiver of Ehlonna and weapons to fill it, an uncommon item priced at 400 gp, in preparation for the job.
- (2025-08-10) Eddie pulled a two-handed sword from it for Chimeg and planned to carry the extra sword in it.
- (2026-08-09) Eddie planned to keep his rapier sheathed in his Quiver of Ehlonna, and Portia, as a spider on his shoulder, was told she could get lost in there.
- (2026-09-06) Eddie brought his quiver and a bunch of weapons on the heist. Kyle ruled it cannot hold a shield (it holds long, slender items), so Eddie's shield counted as carried on his back and needs an action to ready.
- (2026-09-20) Eddie stored the captured Cherek commander's and bearsarks' weapons in the quiver.

chunks.title: Gloves of Thievery
chunks.text:
Item: Gloves of Thievery (first seen 2025-01-19, last seen 2025-07-27)
Type: uncommon magic item (gloves)
Holder: Lucia
Significance: Bought anonymously through a proxy.
- (2025-01-19) Lucia bought Gloves of Thievery through a proxy so the purchase stayed anonymous; Kyle ruled the fee was 25% extra, making it 500 gp instead of 400 gp.
- (2025-05-18) Lucia wore her gloves while disarming a trip line and rolled a 20 on Sleight of Hand.
- (2025-05-18) Lucia picked the giant-sized doors' locks with her gloves on; the first lock needed a crowbar borrowed as a pick, and the GM ruled her picks too small to get the DC 15 so she used a straight roll.
- (2025-06-01) Lucia said her gloves give plus 5 on Sleight of Hand and she has expertise.
- (2025-07-27) Lucia's sleight of hand (a natural 20 on the third tier) locked stones in place for 10 feet of progress.

chunks.title: Goggles of Night
chunks.text:
Item: Goggles of Night (first seen 2025-01-19, last seen 2025-11-02)
Also known as: goggles of light
Type: uncommon magic item (goggles)
Holder: Sir Raf
Properties: Gives Sir Raf darkvision of 60 feet
- (2025-01-19) Sir Raf decided Goggles of Night were a good investment since he lacks darkvision; Monarch said she already has a pair.
- (2025-02-02) Monarch put on goggles at night to examine the fire-giant vial by sight; she wears them (she earlier said she has her own pair).
- (2025-03-02) Monarch left her goggles of night behind for the honor feast so they would not ruin her 15 gp outfit; she brought only her staff.
- (2025-05-04) Sir Raf said he got goggles of night so the party would not need light sources for the ruins.
- (2025-05-04) Monarch joked about trying to fit the goggles of night on her horse.
- (2025-08-24) Sir Raf has darkvision of 60 feet from his Goggles of Night; the GM confirmed it as about 60 feet when he landed in the Hall of Feasts.
- (2025-11-02) Raf said his Goggles of Night already give him darkvision, so he did not need Eddie's Eyes of Night.

chunks.title: Potion of Fire Giant Strength
chunks.text:
Item: Potion of Fire Giant Strength (first seen 2025-02-02, last seen 2025-10-19)
Also known as: vial with flickering flame, potion of giant strength
Type: potion (crystal vial)
Holder: Sir Raf
Properties: Raised Sir Raf's strength; he edited his sheet manually and the boost persisted after he dropped unconscious
Significance: Found in the ankheg nest; the party decided Sir Raf should hold it for emergencies, but he declined to use it for the single combat.
- (2025-02-02) Monarch spotted a crystal vial with a flickering flame inside, jammed in the wall of an ankheg sleeping chamber, and pried it out; it was slightly warm to the touch.
- (2025-02-02) Monarch examined it at night on the edge of camp, sniffed it (sulfur smell) and tasted it with a few fibers of rope; it was warming, invigorating, and made her feel strong.
- (2025-02-02) On an Arcana check Monarch concluded it is a potion of giant strength with a bit of fire giant in the flame.
- (2025-02-02) The party gave the potion to Sir Raf, since high strength would help him, e.g. breaking an ankheg grapple.
- (2025-02-02) Sir Raf decided the single combat with Grock was not life and death and chose not to drink the potion.
- (2025-05-04) Dagha Durok Mazaali Khan offered Sir Raf from the armaments collection two potions of hill giant strength, recovered from the ruins, which set Strength to 21 for an hour; Raf accepted.
- (2025-06-01) Sir Raf said he has potions of giant strength that could help bust open the arcane-locked doors, and offered Lucia one when she worried about her low strength; he said he has two.

chunks.title: Potion of Fire Giant Strength (part 2)
chunks.text:
Item: Potion of Fire Giant Strength (first seen 2025-02-02, last seen 2025-10-19)
- (2025-07-13) Sir Raf drank the potion of fire giant strength before attacking the runestone guardian, saying he wanted every chance he could get.
- (2025-07-13) The GM ruled the potion was still in effect after Sir Raf was knocked unconscious and got back up, since he had not died.
- (2025-10-19) Raf found he carries one frost giant potion and two hill giant strength potions and passed one to Monarch to help hold the rope; plans later redirected a potion toward Eddie for carrying people to the mask.

chunks.title: Ankheg Plates
chunks.text:
Item: Ankheg Plates (first seen 2025-02-02, last seen 2025-02-02)
Also known as: ankheg carapace, Ankeg plates
Type: salvage / crafting material
Holder: Portia
Properties: Dense nonmetal plates; enough for one set of heavy nonmetal armor or two nonmetal shields, saving 50% of cost (750 gp off a 1,500 gp plate set); also usable for medium armor like a breastplate.
Significance: Eddie cures the plates each night so a skilled armorer can make armor, possibly for a druid.
- (2025-02-02) Harvesting the unspent ankheg carcass yielded one vial of acid and enough plates for one set of heavy nonmetal armor or two nonmetal shields, saving 50%.
- (2025-02-02) Portia agreed to carry the plates on her horse.
- (2025-02-02) Eddie works each night at curing and preparing the plates.

chunks.title: Vial of Acid
chunks.text:
Item: Vial of Acid (first seen 2025-02-02, last seen 2025-02-02)
Also known as: acid vial
Type: consumable (acid)
Significance: Collected from the ankheg that had not spewed its acid.
- (2025-02-02) Survival checks on the ankheg carcass yielded enough acid to collect one vial.

chunks.title: Ankheg Nest Gemstones
chunks.text:
Item: Ankheg Nest Gemstones (first seen 2025-02-02, last seen 2025-02-02)
Also known as: nine gemstones, 50 gp gems
Type: gemstones (loot)
Properties: Nine decorative gems such as onyx and bloodstone, valued at 50 gp each.
Significance: Divided evenly among the party and sold or kept at Sun Dragon.
- (2025-02-02) Monarch and Sir Raf pried eight gemstones from the nest walls, nine in total, each worth 50 gp.
- (2025-02-02) The split was 408 gold, one 50 gp gem, and 140 gold contract pay each.

chunks.title: Wing Boots
chunks.text:
Item: Wing Boots (first seen 2025-03-02, last seen 2026-09-20)
Also known as: winged boots, wing boots with converse look
Type: magic boots
Holder: Lucia
Properties: Boots with wings; Lucia describes them as heels with laces, like winged Converse
- (2025-03-02) Lucia wore her wing boots with her dress to the honor feast at Xi'an Palace and joked they were like eighties winged Converse.
- (2025-03-02) Matt says he had AI-generate the wing boots to look good rather than like Doc Martens with wings.
- (2025-05-18) Lucia used her wing boots to fly over the 10-foot ruin stones, hugging the wall after hiding, and flew up to roughly 15 feet to attack the fanatic.
- (2025-07-27) Lucia turned on her boots to fly so she could not fall in the climb; the GM allowed flying that prevented falling but not rising.
- (2026-01-25) Lucia considered activating her boots as a magic action but the boots have charges.
- (2026-05-17) Lucia used her wing boots to fly up the shaft and through the halls, with one hour of flight available.
- (2026-06-14) Lucia activated her boots to fly over the melted river and Monarch followed.
- (2026-09-20) Lucia used her action to activate her wing boots during the air elemental fight.

chunks.title: Luckstone
chunks.text:
Item: Luckstone (first seen 2025-03-02, last seen 2025-06-01)
Also known as: lucky stone
Type: magic stone
Holder: Lucia
Properties: Adds plus one to Lucia's saves and ability checks
- (2025-03-02) Lucia said she has a luckstone that adds plus one, making her charisma roll for the honor feast initiative one lower than her save.
- (2025-06-01) Lucia rubbed her luck stone before prying open the trapped chest lid.

chunks.title: Cult of the Dragon Amulet
chunks.text:
Item: Cult of the Dragon Amulet (first seen 2025-05-04, last seen 2025-10-19)
Also known as: brass amulet, cult amulet, cult symbol
Type: brass amulet / holy symbol
Properties: Flat cut piece of brass with four downward and inward curling fangs topped by a pair of staring eyes and interlaced flames above; plain and inexpensively made
Magic: No arcane feel and no emotional weight; not enchanted
Significance: A second cult symbol was found on a Dawnrealm-attired cult fanatic.
Holder: Portia
- (2025-05-04) Setsen showed Monarch the amulet at the celebration; it was found where the Easterling mage had camped, apparently dropped in his haste to leave.
- (2025-05-04) Monarch's History check identified it as the symbol of the Cult of the Dragon, an old cult tied to Tiamat that sought the favor of chromatic dragons to overthrow the Kingdom of the West; it has no tarnish and no enchantment, so it is of recent manufacture.
- (2025-05-04) Setsen kept the amulet in his possession and let Eddie and Portia study it so they could use it as a familiar object for locate object; Eddie sketched it, and Monarch practiced creating a facsimile with Prestidigitation that would pass casual inspection.
- (2025-05-04) The GM posted an image of the amulet in Miro.
- (2025-05-18) The fanatic, who wore a splash of purple as rank, carried one of the cult symbols like the one found at the camp; the lesser cultists had none. Monarch noted the party no longer had the first symbol since it was not allowed to keep it.

chunks.title: Cult of the Dragon Amulet (part 2)
chunks.text:
Item: Cult of the Dragon Amulet (first seen 2025-05-04, last seen 2025-10-19)
- (2025-10-19) The dead Dreamcaster wore a particularly well-crafted Cult of the Dragon amulet; Portia looted him.

chunks.title: Redhoof
chunks.text:
Item: Redhoof (first seen 2025-05-04, last seen 2025-11-02)
Also known as: war horse
Type: war horse (prize mount)
Holder: Sir Raf
Properties: Improved warhorse: +1 AC, 3 more hit points, +1 to every attribute bonus, advantage on saves against fear
Significance: Prize from Dagha Durok Mazaali Khan for winning the Warrior's Challenge; likes to fight
- (2025-05-04) Dagha Durok Mazaali Khan gifted Sir Raf one of the finest war horses in his stables, named Redhoof, as champion's prize; the GM adjusted its stats.
- (2025-05-04) Redhoof stayed calm during the land shark attack.
- (2025-11-02) Sir Raf wants to bring Redhoof back to Roma. The GM ruled he can keep up if he carries no rider, so Raf will ride rotated horses instead. Raf will buy another riding horse to rotate, and Simona covers the cost.

chunks.title: Stone Camouflage Cloaks and Blankets
chunks.text:
Item: Stone Camouflage Cloaks and Blankets (first seen 2025-05-04, last seen 2025-08-10)
Also known as: gray cloaks, gray blankets, stone colored cloaks
Type: cloaks and blankets
Holder: Eddie
Properties: Broken-pattern gray; advantage on Stealth checks among stone or in stone-like areas
Significance: Given free by the clan for resting in the ruins; Chimeg recommended them
- (2025-05-04) Chimeg advised bringing gray cloaks and blankets to rest unseen; the clan gave them to the party for free.
- (2025-05-04) Eddie noted that he took one of the blankets.
- (2025-08-10) Monarch used a stone camouflage blanket to wrap Black Razor.

chunks.title: Fanatic's Tower of Storms Map and Notes
names: Fanatic's Tower of Storms Map and Notes
chunks.text:
Item: Fanatic's Tower of Storms Map and Notes (first seen 2025-05-18, last seen 2025-10-19)
Also known as: hand-drawn map, Tower of Storms notes
Type: document (hand-drawn map and personal notes)
Holder: Portia
Properties: Shows the route from the entry hall, turning right, to the circled Tower of Storms; notes say its basement should hold a lead to the dragon mask.
Significance: Led the party to the Tower of Storms basement.
- (2025-05-18) The map and notes found on the fanatic mark the spot as the Tower of Storms, once occupied by cloud and storm giant sorcerers and wizards, whose basement she learned was intact.
- (2025-05-18) Portia took the cultists' explorer's pack and planned to copy the map for Chimeg.
- (2025-10-19) The Dreamcaster kept handwritten notes on Qul'drik, incomplete because many scouting parties never returned; they held nothing new and no answer to the portal.

chunks.title: Giants' Manacles of Adamantine-Mithril Alloy
chunks.text:
Item: Giants' Manacles of Adamantine-Mithril Alloy (first seen 2025-05-18, last seen 2025-05-18)
Also known as: runed chains and manacles
Type: restraints
Properties: Alloy of adamant and mithril, every link carved with giant runes related to power transfer.
Significance: Suggests the giants drained power from imprisoned immortals to fuel the towers' binding.
- (2025-05-18) In the prison room, Sir Raf found the manacles were an unusual alloy of adamant and mithril covered in giant runes; his Arcana check suggested power transfer from the prisoners rather than mere binding.

chunks.title: Flaming Ritual Daggers
chunks.text:
Item: Flaming Ritual Daggers (first seen 2025-05-18, last seen 2025-05-18)
Also known as: fiery wavy daggers, ritual sickles
Type: cult weapons
Properties: Wavy blades forged to look like flames that crackle with fire; the fanatic's dagger could split into a floating flaming dagger.
Significance: Their flames were tied to their wielders' life essence.
- (2025-05-18) The cultists drew wavy flame-forged daggers; when they died the flames stopped and the daggers no longer appeared magical, so there was no loot.

chunks.title: Giant-Scale Rune Stone Container
chunks.text:
Item: Giant-Scale Rune Stone Container (first seen 2025-06-01, last seen 2025-06-01)
Also known as: crackling runestone box, rune stone box, room box, runestone
Type: container (rune stone)
Holder: Monarch
Properties: Looks like a giant's rune stone but is unusually light, with a seam like a cleverly designed container; the crackling electricity actually came from the ring inside
Significance: Pulled by Monarch from the shambling mound's vines; carried a giant-sized ring
- (2025-06-01) Monarch found rune stones and book pages wrapped in the shambling mound; one stone marked with the room of storms still crackled with electricity and was buried deep in the vines.
- (2025-06-01) Monarch pulled the stone out by hand; it was unusually light and her Investigation showed it is a cleverly designed container with a seam.
- (2025-06-01) Lucia opened it with a Sleight of Hand 30; inside, cushioned with velvet, was a giant-sized ring, and the crackling electricity came from the ring.

chunks.title: Giant's Crackling Ring
chunks.text:
Item: Giant's Crackling Ring (first seen 2025-06-01, last seen 2026-09-20)
Also known as: giant-sized ring, ring sized for a giant, ring of lightning resistance
Type: ring (magic)
Holder: Sir Raf
Properties: Grants resistance to lightning damage; halved the Fenrir's chain lightning for Sir Raf
Significance: Probably meant for whoever had to wrangle the lightning creature.
Magic: Eddie said it does not require attunement
- (2025-06-01) Found cushioned in velvet inside the rune stone container; Lucia handed it to Monarch to examine.
- (2025-06-15) Monarch cast Identify (using a second-level spell slot) on the ring before the long rest; the GM said it is a ring of lightning resistance, needs no attunement, and halves lightning damage.
- (2025-07-27) Monarch planned to attune to the ring of lightning resistance for the climb, taking two hours.
- (2025-09-21) Eddie is wearing the ring of lightning resistance; Monarch's lightning bolt hit Eddie for 10 after he saved (40 of 45 resisted).
- (2025-10-05) Eddie took only 9 from the half blue dragon's lightning breath because he is lightning resistant.
- (2025-11-02) Monarch said the ring plus the blue dragon mask would give lightning immunity but not the healing yet.
- (2026-09-20) Eddie offered to lend the ring of lightning resistance to Raf and put it into party equipment.
- (2026-09-20) Raf equipped the ring from party inventory. The Fenrir's chain lightning hit him for 39, and he resisted half (took 19) because of the ring.

chunks.title: Cloth-Wrapped Mirror
chunks.text:
Item: Cloth-Wrapped Mirror (first seen 2025-06-01, last seen 2026-07-26)
Also known as: cloth wrapped rectangle, flat object, the mirror, Mirror of the Past, thing under the bearskin
Type: large flat framed object, possibly a mirror or portrait
Holder: Lucia
Properties: Shows scenes from the past of a specific object or creature; the GM said the target must be identifiable as one unique creature
